disclaimer: Reference information only. Symptom links are not diagnoses or estimates of probability. Seek qualified clinical assessment for personal medical concerns.

sources.title: Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency anaemia

conditions.description: Repeated reflux of stomach contents into the oesophagus, commonly causing heartburn or regurgitation.

common: Often after meals, bending or lying down
Sour or acidic fluid reaching the throat or mouth

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often recurrent and meal- or posture-related; symptoms may fluctuate over time.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Burning or regurgitation linked to meals or lying down supports reflux context.
alternative_context
Exertional pressure-like chest discomfort requires cardiovascular consideration.
red_flags: Especially with weight loss, persistent vomiting or anaemia
Severe chest pressure with breathlessness, sweating or collapse
Treat as possible cardiac emergency rather than assuming reflux
common_investigations: Assess symptom pattern and alarm features
Considered for alarm features, refractory symptoms or diagnostic uncertainty
conditions.diagnostic_context: Usually assessed clinically; similar symptoms can arise from cardiac, ulcer, biliary or oesophageal disorders.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Routine reflux is not usually an emergency, but cardiac-pattern chest pain and gastrointestinal bleeding require urgent escalation.
population_context: Can occur at any adult age
Pregnancy can increase reflux

conditions.description: A chronic disorder of gut-brain interaction characterised by recurrent abdominal pain and altered bowel habit without a single structural cause.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Symptoms commonly fluctuate, with episodic flares and variable stool pattern.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Visible blood, persistent fever, progressive weight loss or nocturnal symptoms are not typical IBS features.
characteristic
Pain associated with defecation plus change in stool frequency or form supports an IBS pattern.
red_flags: Requires assessment for causes other than IBS
Unintentional weight loss, persistent fever or progressive symptoms
Especially with family history of bowel cancer or inflammatory bowel disease
common_investigations: Apply symptom criteria and check alarm features
Used selectively to exclude coeliac disease, inflammation, infection or anaemia
conditions.diagnostic_context: A positive symptom-based diagnosis is possible after appropriate assessment; it is not inferred from abdominal symptoms alone.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: IBS can significantly affect quality of life but does not itself cause bleeding or bowel damage.
population_context: Often begins before age 50
Symptoms can affect any sex

conditions.description: An autoimmune condition in which gluten exposure damages the small-intestinal lining in genetically susceptible people.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: May present at any age and persists unless gluten exposure is removed; presentation ranges from gastrointestinal to extra-intestinal.
differentiating_features: alternative_context
IBS-like symptoms can overlap, but coeliac disease has serological and biopsy evidence.
important_negative
Starting a gluten-free diet before testing can reduce test accuracy.
red_flags: Marked weight loss, dehydration or signs of significant malnutrition
common_investigations: Detect relevant antibodies while the person is eating gluten
May confirm diagnosis after specialist assessment
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires testing while consuming gluten and should not be made from symptom response alone.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually non-emergent, but severe dehydration, bleeding or profound weakness needs urgent assessment.
population_context: Can present in childhood or adulthood
Family history increases likelihood

conditions.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Typically relapsing and remitting, with inflammatory flares and quieter periods.
risk_factors: younger age at onset is common
differentiating_features: characteristic
Weight loss, blood, raised inflammatory markers or perianal disease distinguish it from uncomplicated IBS.
alternative_context
Infection can also cause diarrhoea and inflammation and may need exclusion.
red_flags: Severe abdominal distension, vomiting or inability to pass stool or gas
Frequent bloody diarrhoea with fever, severe pain or dehydration
conditions.diagnostic_context: No single symptom establishes Crohn's disease; diagnosis combines clinical, laboratory, endoscopic, histological and imaging findings.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Complications can include obstruction, abscess, fistula and severe bleeding.
population_context: Often begins in adolescence or young adulthood
Can occur at any age

conditions.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting the inner lining of the colon and rectum.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually relapsing and remitting; severity depends on the extent and activity of colonic inflammation.
risk_factors: younger adult age is a common onset period
differentiating_features: characteristic
Visible blood and urgency with objective colonic inflammation distinguish it from IBS.
alternative_context
Infectious colitis can resemble a flare and requires consideration.
red_flags: Six or more bloody stools daily with systemic illness, fever or fast heart rate
Severe distension, pain, fever and marked illness
common_investigations: Confirm continuous colonic inflammation and extent
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires objective evidence of colonic inflammation and exclusion of infection.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Acute severe colitis is a medical emergency requiring hospital assessment.
population_context: Often begins in younger adults
Can occur at any age

conditions.description: A variable inflammatory airway condition causing episodes of reversible airflow limitation and respiratory symptoms.

common: Often worse at night or early morning

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Symptoms vary over time and intensity and may be triggered by viral infections, allergens, exercise, cold air or irritants.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Variable symptoms and objective reversibility or variability in airflow support asthma.
alternative_context
Persistent fixed breathlessness, cardiac symptoms or isolated throat noise may indicate another cause.
red_flags: Severe breathlessness, inability to speak normally, exhaustion, blue lips or poor response to reliever
common_investigations: Look for variable expiratory airflow limitation
May support type 2 airway inflammation in context
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis combines a compatible variable symptom pattern with objective evidence where possible.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: A severe or rapidly worsening attack requires emergency care.
population_context: Can begin in childhood or adulthood
Patterns and triggers vary by person

conditions.description: A progressive lung disease with persistent airflow obstruction, commonly related to long-term exposure to tobacco smoke or other inhaled pollutants.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually in mid or later adulthood and may include acute exacerbations.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Persistent rather than fully variable airflow obstruction supports COPD.
alternative_context
Asthma, heart failure and lung cancer may overlap in presentation.
red_flags: Severe worsening breathlessness, confusion, blue lips or inability to speak normally
Coughing blood or unexplained weight loss
Requires assessment for alternative or complicating disease
common_investigations: Assess alternatives and complications when indicated
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptoms plus exposure history require spirometric confirmation; breathlessness alone is nonspecific.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Exacerbations range from mild to life-threatening.
population_context: Usually diagnosed after age 35
Smoking exposure is common but not universal

conditions.description: An infection acquired outside hospital that inflames the lung air sacs and can range from mild to severe.

common: Often sharp and worse on breathing or coughing

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often acute over hours to days; recovery time varies with organism, age, comorbidity and severity.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Fever, focal chest signs or new infiltrate support pneumonia over uncomplicated bronchitis.
alternative_context
Pulmonary embolism can also cause sudden breathlessness and pleuritic pain.
red_flags: Severe breathing difficulty, blue lips, collapse or new severe confusion
Unable to keep fluids down or markedly reduced urine
common_investigations: Assess oxygen saturation, respiratory rate and severity
Confirm or assess pneumonia when clinically indicated
Used in more severe or uncertain cases
conditions.diagnostic_context: Clinical assessment determines whether imaging and microbiology are needed; cough and fever alone are not specific.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Severity assessment is essential because pneumonia can progress to respiratory failure or sepsis.
population_context: Higher complication risk in infants, older adults and people with comorbidity

conditions.description: Blockage of a pulmonary artery, most often by a blood clot that travelled from a deep vein.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often sudden, though smaller emboli may cause subtler symptoms; untreated disease can deteriorate rapidly.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Sudden breathlessness with pleuritic pain and venous-thrombosis risk factors raises concern.
important_negative
A normal symptom description alone cannot safely exclude pulmonary embolism.
red_flags: Sudden breathlessness or pleuritic chest pain with fainting, coughing blood or one-sided leg swelling
common_investigations: Guide imaging in appropriate low/intermediate-risk contexts
ECG, oxygen saturation and blood tests
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires formal clinical probability assessment and appropriate testing; consumer symptom matching is unsafe.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Potentially life-threatening emergency.
population_context: Risk rises with age and acquired risk factors
Can occur without an obvious provoking factor

conditions.description: Persistently elevated arterial blood pressure, usually without symptoms but associated with long-term cardiovascular and kidney risk.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually and persists unless addressed; detection depends on measurement rather than symptoms.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Headache or dizziness does not diagnose hypertension.
characteristic
Repeated properly taken blood-pressure measurements establish the pattern.
red_flags: Very high blood pressure with chest pain, severe breathlessness, neurological deficit, confusion or vision loss
Possible hypertensive emergency or another acute vascular event
common_investigations: Repeated clinic and home or ambulatory blood pressure
Blood, urine and cardiovascular risk assessment
Look for organ effects, causes and overall risk
conditions.diagnostic_context: Requires repeated validated measurements and clinical interpretation; single readings can be misleading.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most hypertension is managed non-emergently; acute symptoms with severe elevation require emergency assessment.
population_context: Prevalence increases with age
Thresholds and targets depend on clinical context

conditions.description: A supraventricular arrhythmia with disorganised atrial electrical activity and an irregular ventricular rhythm.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: May be episodic, persistent or permanent; episodes can start and stop unpredictably.
differentiating_features: characteristic
An irregularly irregular rhythm on ECG supports atrial fibrillation.
alternative_context
Anxiety, ectopic beats and other arrhythmias can all produce palpitations.
red_flags: Palpitations with sudden facial droop, limb weakness or speech difficulty
Fast irregular heartbeat with chest pain, severe breathlessness, collapse or shock
conditions.diagnostic_context: Pulse or wearable alerts can prompt assessment but diagnosis requires an interpretable rhythm recording.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Urgency depends on haemodynamic symptoms, stroke features and rate; stroke-risk assessment is clinically important.
population_context: More common with increasing age
Can occur in younger adults

conditions.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of coronary arteries that may cause stable angina or acute coronary syndromes.

common: Often provoked by exertion in stable angina
possible: Discomfort radiating to arm, jaw, back or upper abdomen

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Chronic disease may be silent or cause reproducible exertional symptoms; plaque disruption can cause an acute emergency.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Pressure-like exertional discomfort relieved by rest is a typical stable-angina pattern.
alternative_context
Musculoskeletal, reflux and anxiety-related chest symptoms can overlap but must not be assumed without assessment.
red_flags: New, severe or persistent chest pressure, especially with breathlessness, sweating, nausea or radiation
common_investigations: Assess stable suspected disease in selected patients
Assess lipids, glucose and related risk
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptom pattern informs urgency, but ECG, biomarkers and/or imaging are required for diagnosis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Possible acute coronary syndrome is an emergency.
population_context: Risk increases with age and vascular risk burden
Presentations may be less typical in some women, older adults and people with diabetes

conditions.description: A clinical syndrome in which cardiac function is insufficient to meet the body's needs without elevated filling pressures.

common: On exertion or when lying flat

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: May develop gradually or present acutely; chronic symptoms often fluctuate with fluid status and precipitating illness.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Orthopnoea, raised jugular venous pressure, oedema and objective cardiac abnormalities support heart failure.
alternative_context
Lung disease, anaemia and deconditioning can also cause exertional breathlessness.
red_flags: Severe breathlessness at rest, frothy sputum, blue lips, collapse or confusion
Rapidly increasing swelling, weight or breathlessness
common_investigations: Help assess likelihood in suspected chronic heart failure
ECG, chest imaging and blood tests
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptoms are nonspecific; diagnosis requires objective evidence of cardiac dysfunction or raised filling pressures.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Acute pulmonary oedema or shock is an emergency.
population_context: More common with increasing age
Can occur at any age with cardiomyopathy or congenital disease

conditions.description: A recurrent neurological disorder with episodic headache and associated sensory symptoms, sometimes preceded by aura.

common: Often pulsating and one-sided, but not always

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Attacks usually evolve over minutes and last hours to days; frequency varies widely.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Recurrent attacks with nausea or light/sound sensitivity support migraine.
important_negative
Sudden maximal-at-onset headache, persistent focal deficit, fever with neck stiffness or a new pattern is not routine migraine.
red_flags: Sudden explosive headache reaching maximum intensity rapidly
Possible subarachnoid haemorrhage or other acute cause
New headache with persistent weakness, speech difficulty, seizure, confusion or loss of vision
common_investigations: Clinical headache history and neurological examination
Identify migraine pattern and red flags
Reserved for red flags, abnormal examination or atypical presentation
conditions.diagnostic_context: Migraine is diagnosed clinically after considering secondary headache causes; aura symptoms are fully reversible and time-limited.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Typical recurrent migraine is not an emergency, but red-flag headache patterns require immediate assessment.
population_context: Often begins in adolescence or early adulthood
More prevalent in women after puberty

conditions.description: A peripheral vestibular disorder in which displaced inner-ear crystals provoke brief vertigo with particular head movements.

common: Triggered by rolling in bed, looking up or other head movement

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Attacks are usually brief, recurrent and position-triggered; episodes may resolve but recur.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Seconds-long vertigo reproducibly triggered by head position supports BPPV.
important_negative
Persistent vertigo with new neurological deficit, severe headache or inability to walk is not typical BPPV.
red_flags: Vertigo with facial droop, limb weakness, speech difficulty, severe new headache or inability to stand
common_investigations: Elicit characteristic nystagmus in the appropriate canal
Check for central or alternative vestibular causes
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis depends on characteristic positional history and examination; dizziness without spinning is broader and nonspecific.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: BPPV itself is benign but increases fall risk; central neurological mimics can be urgent.
population_context: More common in older adults
Can follow head injury

conditions.description: Acute neurological dysfunction caused by interrupted cerebral blood flow or bleeding; transient symptoms may represent a TIA.

possible: Sudden vision loss or double vision

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually sudden onset; symptoms may persist in stroke or resolve in TIA, but both require urgent assessment.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Sudden focal loss of neurological function is the key pattern.
important_negative
Symptom resolution does not make a suspected TIA safe to ignore.
red_flags: Any sudden facial droop, arm weakness or speech difficulty
Sudden severe imbalance, double vision, swallowing difficulty or limb incoordination
common_investigations: Urgent neurological assessment and brain imaging
conditions.diagnostic_context: Time-critical clinical and imaging assessment is required; a symptom index must never rank this as routine self-diagnosis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Always an emergency when current; suspected recent TIA also needs urgent specialist assessment.
population_context: Risk increases with age but stroke can occur at any age

conditions.description: A neurological disorder characterised by an enduring tendency to recurrent unprovoked seizures.

possible: Brief loss or alteration of awareness

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Can begin at any age; seizure type and frequency vary and may change over time.
common_associations: sleep disruption can lower seizure threshold
differentiating_features: important_negative
A single provoked event or faint does not by itself establish epilepsy.
alternative_context
Syncope, sleep disorders, migraine and functional seizures can mimic epileptic events.
red_flags: A seizure lasting about five minutes or repeated seizures without recovery
First suspected seizure, serious injury, pregnancy or incomplete recovery
common_investigations: Detailed event history and witness account
Look for structural or metabolic causes when indicated
conditions.diagnostic_context: Specialist diagnosis integrates history, examination and targeted tests; a normal EEG does not automatically exclude epilepsy.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Prolonged seizures, repeated seizures without recovery or major injury are emergencies.
population_context: Incidence is higher in children and older adults but any age can be affected

conditions.description: A chronic metabolic condition characterised by hyperglycaemia due to insulin resistance and progressive beta-cell dysfunction.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually; prolonged hyperglycaemia can damage blood vessels, nerves, eyes and kidneys.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Thirst or fatigue alone is nonspecific.
characteristic
Persistent laboratory hyperglycaemia is required for diagnosis.
red_flags: Marked thirst and urination with vomiting, dehydration, drowsiness or deep breathing
common_investigations: Urine, kidney, lipid, eye and foot assessment
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis uses validated laboratory thresholds, usually confirmed when the person is not acutely symptomatic.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most cases are non-emergent at detection; hyperglycaemic crisis is an emergency.
population_context: Increasingly occurs in younger adults and adolescents
Risk patterns vary across populations

conditions.description: An autoimmune condition causing severe insulin deficiency through destruction of pancreatic beta cells.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often develops over days to weeks and requires lifelong insulin; onset can occur at any age.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Rapid four-T pattern—thirst, toilet, tiredness and becoming thinner—is characteristic.
alternative_context
Type 2 diabetes and other causes of hyperglycaemia require classification by clinicians.
red_flags: Vomiting, abdominal pain, deep breathing, fruity breath, dehydration, confusion or drowsiness
common_investigations: Immediate capillary or plasma glucose and ketones
Support diagnosis and classification in context
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptomatic marked hyperglycaemia needs same-day assessment; autoantibodies and clinical course help distinguish diabetes type.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Diabetic ketoacidosis is life-threatening and may be the first presentation.
population_context: Commonly begins in children or young adults but can begin at any age

conditions.description: Insufficient thyroid hormone activity causing a general slowing of metabolic processes.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually and may be difficult to recognise from symptoms alone.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Fatigue and weight change are nonspecific without thyroid blood-test abnormalities.
red_flags: Profound drowsiness, hypothermia, slow breathing or collapse in severe hypothyroidism
common_investigations: May identify autoimmune cause when useful
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires biochemical testing interpreted with illness, pregnancy and medication context.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually develops slowly; decompensated severe hypothyroidism is rare but emergent.
population_context: More common in women and with increasing age
Pregnancy has specific testing and treatment considerations

conditions.description: Excess thyroid hormone activity producing increased metabolic and sympathetic effects.

possible: Eye prominence or irritation in Graves disease

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: May develop gradually or over weeks; course depends on cause such as Graves disease, nodules or thyroiditis.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Anxiety and palpitations alone do not establish thyroid disease.
characteristic
Suppressed TSH with elevated thyroid hormones supports overt hyperthyroidism.
red_flags: High fever, marked fast heart rate, agitation, confusion, vomiting or collapse
common_investigations: TSH, free T4 and sometimes free T3
conditions.diagnostic_context: Biochemical confirmation and cause assessment are required; acute illness can alter thyroid tests.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Thyroid storm is rare and life-threatening.
population_context: More common in women
Can occur at any age

conditions.description: Pain between the lower ribs and buttocks without evidence of a specific serious structural or systemic cause.

common: Pain influenced by movement or position

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often improves over days to weeks but can recur or persist; symptom intensity does not directly measure tissue damage.
risk_factors: sleep and psychosocial factors can influence persistence
differentiating_features: important_negative
Progressive neurological loss, saddle numbness, bladder dysfunction, fever or major trauma is not routine non-specific back pain.
alternative_context
Leg-dominant dermatomal pain may indicate radiculopathy.
red_flags: New urinary retention or incontinence, saddle numbness or rapidly progressive bilateral leg weakness
Back pain with fever, major trauma, cancer history or severe unremitting night pain
common_investigations: Usually reserved for red flags, major trauma or when results would change management
conditions.diagnostic_context: Most acute low back pain is diagnosed clinically after excluding specific serious causes; routine imaging can show incidental changes.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most episodes are not emergencies; neurological or systemic red flags change urgency.
population_context: Very common across adulthood

conditions.description: Pain and/or neurological symptoms arising from irritation or compression of a lumbar or sacral nerve root.

common: Often below the knee in a nerve-root distribution

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often acute or subacute and may improve over weeks to months; deficits and course vary by affected root and cause.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Dermatomal leg pain with matching sensory, reflex or strength findings supports radiculopathy.
alternative_context
Peripheral neuropathy, hip disease and vascular claudication can mimic leg symptoms.
red_flags: Saddle numbness, bladder or bowel dysfunction, or rapidly worsening bilateral weakness
New or progressive objective limb weakness
common_investigations: Map strength, sensation and reflex changes
Used when red flags, progressive deficit or persistent symptoms may change management
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis is clinical; imaging findings must match symptoms because disc changes are common without pain.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Pain alone is usually non-emergent; cauda equina symptoms or progressive motor deficit are urgent.
population_context: Common in working-age and older adults

conditions.description: A systemic autoimmune inflammatory disease that primarily affects synovial joints.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often develops over weeks, typically with persistent symmetric small-joint inflammation; untreated disease can damage joints.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Persistent synovitis, prolonged morning stiffness and symmetric small-joint involvement support inflammatory arthritis.
alternative_context
Osteoarthritis typically has briefer stiffness and more load-related pain.
red_flags: One acutely hot, very painful swollen joint with fever or systemic illness
Possible septic arthritis rather than routine flare
Neck pain with new weakness, gait change or bladder symptoms
common_investigations: Inflammatory markers, rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP
Support diagnosis and prognosis in context
conditions.diagnostic_context: Early specialist assessment is important; negative antibodies do not exclude seronegative rheumatoid arthritis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually not an emergency, but infection or neurological complications require urgent assessment.
population_context: More common in women
Often begins between ages 30 and 60 but any age can be affected

conditions.description: A whole-joint disorder involving cartilage, bone and surrounding tissues, commonly causing activity-related pain and stiffness.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually and fluctuates; structural severity and pain intensity may not closely match.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Activity-related pain and short-lived morning stiffness are typical.
alternative_context
Prolonged morning stiffness, systemic illness or marked warmth suggests inflammatory or infectious disease.
red_flags: Sudden hot swollen joint with fever or severe illness
Possible joint infection or crystal arthritis
common_investigations: Used when diagnosis is uncertain or planning intervention; not always required
conditions.diagnostic_context: Often diagnosed clinically in a typical presentation; imaging is not a direct measure of pain.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually chronic and non-emergent.
population_context: Prevalence rises with age
Can develop earlier after injury

conditions.description: A chronic relapsing inflammatory skin condition with itch and impaired skin barrier function.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often begins in childhood and fluctuates with flares and remission, though adult-onset disease occurs.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Chronic itch, dryness and typical flexural distribution support atopic dermatitis.
alternative_context
Contact dermatitis, scabies, psoriasis and fungal infection can mimic eczema.
red_flags: Rapidly worsening painful eczema with clustered blisters, punched-out sores, fever or eye involvement
Weeping, crusting, warmth, increasing pain or fever
common_investigations: Usually sufficient in a typical presentation
Used selectively when infection or alternative diagnosis is suspected
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis is clinical and should consider distribution, chronicity, itch and alternatives.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most flares are not emergencies; widespread herpes infection or eye involvement is urgent.
population_context: Common in children
May persist or begin in adulthood

conditions.description: A chronic immune-mediated disease causing accelerated skin-cell turnover and well-demarcated inflamed plaques.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Chronic relapsing course with variable severity and triggers.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Sharply bordered plaques with silvery scale on extensor surfaces are typical.
alternative_context
Eczema, fungal infection and seborrhoeic dermatitis can overlap.
red_flags: Most of the skin becomes red, painful or sheds with fever or systemic illness
Persistent swollen joints, prolonged stiffness or dactylitis
conditions.diagnostic_context: Usually clinical; atypical lesions may require dermatology review or biopsy.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most disease is non-emergent; generalised pustular or erythrodermic forms can be severe.
population_context: Can begin at any age
Family history is common

conditions.description: A bacterial infection of deeper skin and subcutaneous tissues causing a spreading area of inflammation.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops over hours to days and may spread without treatment.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Unilateral expanding warmth, tenderness and redness support cellulitis.
alternative_context
Venous stasis, contact dermatitis and deep-vein thrombosis can mimic it.
red_flags: Rapid spread with severe pain, confusion, fast breathing, collapse or mottled skin
Cellulitis around the eye or central face
common_investigations: Assess extent, entry site and severity
Used for systemic illness, unusual exposures or severe infection
conditions.diagnostic_context: Usually diagnosed clinically; bilateral red legs without systemic features often have non-infectious causes.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Can progress to abscess, sepsis or deeper infection.
population_context: Risk increases with oedema, skin breaks and immune compromise

conditions.description: Transient raised itchy wheals caused by superficial dermal swelling, with or without deeper angioedema.

common: Individual lesions usually fade within 24 hours
possible: Deeper swelling of lips, eyelids or hands

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Acute episodes last days to weeks; chronic urticaria recurs for more than six weeks and is often not due to food allergy.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Migratory wheals that disappear without bruising are typical.
important_negative
A fixed painful lesion lasting over 24 hours or leaving bruising suggests another process.
red_flags: Hives or swelling with breathing difficulty, throat tightness, wheeze, collapse or severe dizziness
common_investigations: Only when history suggests a specific allergy or systemic cause
conditions.diagnostic_context: Appearance and transient course are key; broad allergy panels are not routinely diagnostic for chronic spontaneous urticaria.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Skin-only hives are usually not an emergency; airway, breathing or circulatory symptoms are.
population_context: Can occur at any age

conditions.description: An acute respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often begins abruptly; uncomplicated symptoms commonly improve over several days though cough and fatigue may persist.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Abrupt fever, aches and marked fatigue are more typical than in a mild cold.
alternative_context
COVID-19 and other respiratory viruses overlap substantially and may require testing.
red_flags: Severe breathing difficulty, blue lips, chest pain, collapse or confusion
Worsening after initial improvement or inability to hydrate in a high-risk person
common_investigations: Used when results affect infection control or clinical decisions
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptoms overlap with other infections; laboratory confirmation may be needed in selected settings.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most illness is self-limited, but severe respiratory or neurological complications occur.
population_context: Higher complication risk in very young or older people, pregnancy and chronic disease

conditions.description: An infectious disease caused by SARS-CoV-2 with presentations ranging from asymptomatic infection to severe multisystem illness.

possible: New loss or change of smell or taste

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Symptoms commonly begin days after exposure and vary by variant, immunity and host factors; a minority develop persistent post-acute symptoms.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Symptoms alone cannot reliably distinguish COVID-19 from influenza or other respiratory infections.
red_flags: Severe breathing difficulty, persistent chest pain, new confusion, inability to wake or blue/grey lips
Possible severe COVID-19 or another emergency
common_investigations: Detect current infection depending on timing and test
conditions.diagnostic_context: Testing and clinical context are needed because symptom overlap is broad and test sensitivity depends on timing.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Severity ranges widely; acute respiratory compromise is an emergency.
population_context: Can affect all ages
Risk of severe disease rises with age and some conditions

conditions.description: Reactivation of varicella-zoster virus in a sensory nerve distribution.

common: Burning, tingling or pain on one side

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Pain or tingling may precede rash; lesions crust over in weeks, while nerve pain can persist.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Painful unilateral dermatomal blisters that usually do not cross the midline are typical.
alternative_context
Contact dermatitis and herpes simplex may resemble the rash.
red_flags: Rash on forehead, nose or around the eye, eye pain or vision change
Widespread rash or systemic illness in an immunocompromised person
common_investigations: Used when presentation is atypical or diagnosis important
conditions.diagnostic_context: Usually clinical; pain without rash has a broad differential and cannot be assigned to shingles by symptoms alone.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Eye, ear, neurological or disseminated involvement requires urgent assessment.
population_context: Incidence and complications rise with age and immune compromise

conditions.description: A syndrome usually caused by primary Epstein-Barr virus infection, particularly symptomatic in adolescents and young adults.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Acute throat and fever symptoms often improve in weeks, while fatigue may persist longer.
risk_factors: adolescence or young adulthood for symptomatic disease
differentiating_features: characteristic
Prominent posterior neck nodes, fatigue and compatible blood findings support mononucleosis.
alternative_context
Streptococcal tonsillitis and acute HIV can produce similar syndromes.
red_flags: Sudden severe left upper abdominal or shoulder-tip pain, dizziness or collapse
Difficulty breathing, drooling or inability to swallow fluids
common_investigations: Full blood count and heterophile or EBV serology
Support diagnosis in the appropriate illness phase
conditions.diagnostic_context: Test performance depends on timing and age; alternative causes of mononucleosis-like illness may need consideration.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most recover without emergency care, but airway obstruction and splenic rupture are rare serious complications.
population_context: Symptomatic disease is commonest in adolescents and young adults

conditions.description: IgE-mediated inflammation of the nasal lining after exposure to an allergen.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Symptoms may be seasonal or perennial and recur with exposure.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Itch, sneezing and clear discharge linked to exposure support allergy.
alternative_context
Fever, marked malaise and purulent discharge suggest infection rather than uncomplicated allergy.
common_investigations: Relate symptoms to exposures and season
Used when identifying a relevant trigger would change management
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis is often clinical; a positive allergy test indicates sensitisation and must match symptoms.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually non-emergent, though associated asthma symptoms require separate severity assessment.
population_context: Common in children and adults

conditions.description: An adverse immune response to a food; immediate IgE-mediated reactions can involve skin, gut, airway or circulation.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Immediate reactions usually begin within minutes to a few hours of exposure; non-IgE patterns may be delayed.
differentiating_features: characteristic
A reproducible, time-linked multisystem reaction supports immediate food allergy.
alternative_context
Food intolerance does not involve the same immune mechanism and usually does not cause anaphylaxis.
red_flags: Airway swelling, breathing difficulty, collapse or rapidly progressive multisystem reaction after food
common_investigations: Support suspected immediate allergy when matched to history
Reference standard in selected specialist settings
conditions.diagnostic_context: Broad panel testing without a compatible history can produce misleading sensitisation results.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Anaphylaxis is an emergency; prior reaction severity does not perfectly predict the next reaction.
population_context: Common foods and natural history differ by age

conditions.description: A severe, rapidly developing systemic hypersensitivity reaction that can compromise airway, breathing or circulation.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually begins within minutes of exposure but timing varies; symptoms can progress rapidly.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Skin findings may be absent; airway, breathing or circulatory compromise after likely exposure is sufficient concern.
alternative_context
Panic can cause breathlessness and tingling but does not cause objective airway swelling, wheeze, hives or hypotension.
red_flags: Sudden airway swelling, wheeze, breathing difficulty, collapse or severe dizziness after a possible trigger
common_investigations: Diagnosis and treatment are primarily clinical and time-critical
May support mechanism later in selected cases
conditions.diagnostic_context: Do not delay emergency action for testing when anaphylaxis is suspected.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Always a medical emergency.
population_context: Can occur at any age

conditions.description: Inflammation of skin caused by direct irritation or delayed allergic sensitivity to a contacting substance.

common: Red or discoloured rash at contact sites

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Develops after exposure and improves when the relevant irritant or allergen is avoided, though chronic occupational exposure can sustain it.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Distribution matching contact exposure supports the diagnosis.
alternative_context
Fungal infection, psoriasis and atopic eczema may overlap.
red_flags: Rapidly increasing pain, warmth, pus or fever
common_investigations: Identify delayed contact allergy in persistent or suspected allergic cases
conditions.diagnostic_context: The timing and distribution of exposure matter; patch tests do not diagnose irritant dermatitis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually non-emergent unless severe infection or systemic allergic symptoms develop.
population_context: Occupational patterns are common in healthcare, cleaning, hairdressing and food work

conditions.description: Infection affecting the bladder or urethra, most commonly bacterial.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually acute over hours to days; symptoms may ascend to involve the kidneys.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Vaginal discharge or prominent irritation suggests an alternative genital cause.
alternative_context
Fever with flank pain suggests upper urinary infection rather than simple cystitis.
red_flags: Fever, flank pain, vomiting or systemic illness with urinary symptoms
Confusion, collapse, very fast breathing or mottled skin
common_investigations: Used for pregnancy, recurrent/complicated infection, treatment failure or uncertain cases
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptom combinations and patient context guide diagnosis; urine findings without symptoms do not always represent infection.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Simple lower UTI is usually non-emergent; pyelonephritis or sepsis requires urgent care.
population_context: More common in women
UTI in pregnancy, men, children or frail older adults needs context-specific assessment

conditions.description: Crystalline stones forming in the urinary tract, which may obstruct urine flow and cause renal colic.

common: Often waves and may radiate to groin
possible: Urinary urgency with a distal stone

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Pain often begins suddenly and fluctuates as a stone moves; small stones may pass, while obstruction can persist.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Colicky flank-to-groin pain with haematuria is typical.
alternative_context
Aortic, gastrointestinal, gynaecological and musculoskeletal emergencies can mimic renal colic.
red_flags: Fever or rigors with suspected stone pain
Anuria, known single kidney, pregnancy or uncontrolled pain/vomiting
common_investigations: Assess blood, infection and renal function
Locate stone and obstruction depending on context
conditions.diagnostic_context: Imaging confirms stone and obstruction when required; not all flank pain is renal colic.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Infected obstruction threatens kidney function and can cause sepsis.
population_context: Commonest in adults
Recurrence is frequent

conditions.description: Persistent abnormalities of kidney structure or function with implications for health.

possible: Shortness of breath in advanced disease

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually progresses slowly or remains stable; early disease is detected by blood and urine testing rather than symptoms.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Normal urine appearance and absence of pain do not exclude CKD.
characteristic
Persistent reduced eGFR or markers of kidney damage for at least three months define chronicity.
red_flags: Very low urine output, rapidly increasing swelling, breathlessness, confusion or severe weakness
Possible acute kidney injury or advanced complication
conditions.diagnostic_context: Single abnormal eGFR does not prove CKD; persistence and clinical context are required.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most CKD is chronic and monitored; acute deterioration, hyperkalaemia or pulmonary oedema may be emergent.
population_context: Risk rises with age and cardiometabolic disease

conditions.description: A group of syndromes involving prostate or pelvic pain and urinary symptoms, including acute bacterial and chronic forms.

possible: Difficulty starting or maintaining urine flow

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Acute bacterial disease starts rapidly with systemic illness; chronic pelvic pain forms persist or recur over months.
differentiating_features: characteristic
High fever and marked illness distinguish acute bacterial prostatitis from chronic pelvic pain syndrome.
alternative_context
UTI, urethritis, stones and testicular disorders can overlap.
red_flags: Fever, rigors, severe pelvic pain or systemic illness with urinary symptoms
Possible acute bacterial prostatitis or sepsis
common_investigations: Clinical genital, abdominal and selective prostate assessment
conditions.diagnostic_context: The label covers distinct acute infectious and chronic pain syndromes; evaluation should distinguish them.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Acute bacterial prostatitis can cause sepsis and urinary retention.
population_context: Occurs in people with a prostate across adult ages

conditions.description: Persistent, excessive and difficult-to-control worry across multiple areas of life, accompanied by distress or functional impairment.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Symptoms are persistent rather than confined to discrete attacks and often fluctuate with stress.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Broad persistent worry on most days differs from brief, unexpected panic attacks.
important_negative
Physical symptoms should not automatically be attributed to anxiety without appropriate medical context.
red_flags: Immediate intent or plan to self-harm, inability to stay safe, or severe crisis
common_investigations: Assess duration, impairment, comorbidity and risk
Consider thyroid, medication, substance and other medical contributors when indicated
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires duration, excessiveness, distress/impairment and exclusion of better explanations; worry alone is common and not diagnostic.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most care is non-emergent; immediate safety concerns change urgency.
population_context: Can affect children and adults
Presentations vary culturally and by age

conditions.description: Recurrent unexpected panic attacks followed by persistent concern or behaviour change related to further attacks.

common: Abrupt surge of intense fear or discomfort

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Attacks peak rapidly and resolve, while anticipatory anxiety and avoidance may persist between episodes.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Recurrent unexpected attacks plus ongoing concern/avoidance distinguish panic disorder from an isolated panic attack.
important_negative
First or atypical chest pain, syncope, objective neurological change or exertional symptoms require medical consideration.
red_flags: Chest pressure with exertion, collapse, severe persistent breathlessness or focal neurological deficit
Do not assume panic; assess possible medical emergency
Immediate risk of self-harm or inability to stay safe
common_investigations: Assess attack pattern, avoidance, impairment and risk
Consider cardiac, respiratory, endocrine or substance causes based on presentation
conditions.diagnostic_context: Panic symptoms are real but nonspecific; diagnosis follows appropriate exclusion of acute medical causes when indicated.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Panic attacks are not inherently dangerous, but mimics and safety risks must be recognised.
population_context: Often begins in adolescence or early adulthood

conditions.description: A mood disorder involving persistent depressed mood or loss of interest with additional cognitive, physical and functional changes.

uncommon: Mood-congruent psychotic symptoms in severe depression

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Episodes last at least weeks and may be single or recurrent; severity and recovery vary.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Normal short-lived sadness without sustained impairment is not automatically a depressive disorder.
alternative_context
Past mania or hypomania changes the diagnostic context toward bipolar disorder.
red_flags: Current suicidal intent, plan, recent attempt or inability to remain safe
Severe self-neglect, psychosis, stupor or inability to eat or drink
common_investigations: Assess symptoms, duration, impairment and risk
Consider thyroid, anaemia, medicines and other contributors when appropriate
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires a sustained syndrome with distress or impairment and assessment for bipolarity, substances, grief and medical contributors.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Urgency is driven by suicide risk, psychosis, severe self-neglect and inability to function safely.
population_context: Can affect any age
Perinatal and older-adult presentations need context

conditions.description: A mood disorder characterised by episodes of mania or hypomania and usually episodes of depression.

common: Distinct elevated or markedly irritable mood during mania/hypomania

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Episodic course with periods of mood disturbance and recovery; episode frequency and polarity vary.
risk_factors: some substances or medicines can precipitate symptoms
differentiating_features: characteristic
Reduced need for sleep with sustained increased energy differs from insomnia with fatigue.
important_negative
Ordinary mood variation or brief excitement does not constitute mania or hypomania.
red_flags: Severe agitation, psychosis, dangerous impulsivity, inability to care for self or several nights without sleep
Possible severe mania requiring urgent assessment
Current suicidal intent, plan or inability to stay safe
common_investigations: Establish episode duration, impairment, polarity and collateral history
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis requires evidence of mania or hypomania and careful longitudinal assessment; depressive symptoms alone cannot identify bipolar disorder.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Severe mania, psychosis and suicide risk may require emergency care.
population_context: Often begins in adolescence or early adulthood
Can present later

conditions.description: Inflammation of the nasal and paranasal sinus lining, most often following a viral upper-respiratory infection.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often resolves within a few weeks; prolonged or worsening symptoms may indicate bacterial disease or another diagnosis.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Facial pain without nasal symptoms is less typical of sinusitis.
alternative_context
Migraine commonly causes facial pressure and nasal autonomic symptoms.
red_flags: Eye swelling, reduced eye movement, double vision or reduced vision
Severe frontal headache with confusion, neck stiffness or focal neurological symptoms
common_investigations: Usually sufficient for uncomplicated acute disease
Reserved for complications, recurrent atypical disease or surgical planning
conditions.diagnostic_context: Coloured mucus alone does not prove bacterial infection; duration, severity and pattern matter.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most cases are self-limited; orbital and intracranial complications are rare but urgent.
population_context: Common after viral infections in adults and children

conditions.description: Acute infection and inflammation of the middle ear, commonly following an upper-respiratory infection.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually acute and often improves within days; fluid-related hearing reduction can last longer.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Bulging inflamed eardrum on otoscopy supports acute otitis media.
alternative_context
Outer-ear infection causes canal tenderness and a different examination pattern.
red_flags: Swelling, redness or tenderness behind the ear with the ear pushed forward
Facial weakness, severe vertigo or marked systemic illness
common_investigations: Used for persistent hearing difficulty or recurrent disease
conditions.diagnostic_context: Ear pain alone is nonspecific; otoscopic findings distinguish middle-ear infection from other causes.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually self-limited; mastoid or neurological complications require urgent care.
population_context: Particularly common in young children

conditions.description: Perception of sound without a corresponding external source; it may be subjective or rarely pulse-synchronous.

common: Ringing, buzzing, humming or other phantom sound

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: May be transient, intermittent or chronic; impact varies substantially.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Pulse-synchronous tinnitus has a different vascular differential from steady subjective tinnitus.
alternative_context
Earwax, infection and temporomandibular disorders can contribute.
red_flags: Pulsatile unilateral tinnitus or tinnitus with focal neurological signs
common_investigations: Used for unilateral, pulsatile or neurological presentations when indicated
conditions.diagnostic_context: Tinnitus is a symptom with many causes; laterality, pulsatility, hearing change and examination guide evaluation.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually non-emergent, but sudden hearing loss and focal neurological signs are urgent.
population_context: More common with age and cumulative noise exposure

conditions.description: Acute inflammation of the tonsils, most often viral but sometimes bacterial.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually begins acutely and resolves within days; persistent, recurrent or asymmetric symptoms require reassessment.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Cough and coryza favour viral infection but are not definitive.
alternative_context
Severe unilateral symptoms, trismus or muffled voice may indicate peritonsillar abscess.
red_flags: Breathing difficulty, drooling, inability to swallow, stridor or rapidly worsening neck swelling
Severe one-sided throat pain, muffled voice or difficulty opening the mouth
common_investigations: Used selectively according to local guidance and context
conditions.diagnostic_context: Appearance alone cannot reliably distinguish viral from bacterial tonsillitis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most cases are self-limited; airway compromise and deep-neck infection are urgent.
population_context: Common in children and young adults

conditions.description: Inflammation of the conjunctiva caused by infection, allergy or irritation.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often acute; viral and bacterial forms can spread, while allergic episodes recur with exposure.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Severe pain, marked light sensitivity, reduced vision or a cloudy cornea is not typical simple conjunctivitis.
alternative_context
Uveitis, keratitis and acute glaucoma can also cause a red eye.
red_flags: Red eye with pain, light sensitivity, reduced vision, trauma or contact-lens-related pain
common_investigations: Distinguish uncomplicated conjunctivitis from deeper eye disease
Reserved for severe, recurrent, neonatal or treatment-resistant infection
conditions.diagnostic_context: Discharge pattern suggests but does not reliably prove cause; vision and pain assessment are essential.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most conjunctivitis is non-emergent; painful visual change requires urgent eye assessment.
population_context: Occurs at all ages
Neonatal conjunctivitis needs urgent assessment

conditions.description: A multifactorial ocular-surface disorder involving tear-film instability and eye discomfort.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often chronic and fluctuating, worsened by prolonged visual tasks, dry environments or reduced blinking.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Fluctuating discomfort and blur that changes with blinking supports tear-film instability.
important_negative
Severe pain, fixed visual loss or a markedly red eye suggests another diagnosis.
red_flags: Severe pain, marked light sensitivity, reduced vision or contact-lens-related red eye
common_investigations: Assess ocular surface and alternative disease
conditions.diagnostic_context: Symptoms and surface signs may not correlate closely; examination helps distinguish dry eye from allergy, infection and corneal disease.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually chronic and non-emergent; corneal warning signs are urgent.
population_context: More common with age
Screen work and contact lenses can aggravate symptoms

conditions.description: Sudden obstruction of aqueous drainage causing a rapid rise in intraocular pressure and risk of permanent vision loss.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually sudden and rapidly progressive over hours.
risk_factors: some pupil-dilating medicines in susceptible eyes
differentiating_features: characteristic
Severe painful red eye with visual blur/halos and nausea is characteristic.
important_negative
Chronic open-angle glaucoma is usually painless and asymptomatic until late.
red_flags: Sudden severe painful red eye with reduced vision, halos, headache or vomiting
common_investigations: Visual acuity, intraocular pressure and slit-lamp examination
Confirm acute pressure elevation and anterior-segment findings
Assess angle anatomy when safe and appropriate
conditions.diagnostic_context: This is a clinical eye emergency; symptom search must prioritise urgency rather than diagnostic ranking.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Sight-threatening emergency.
population_context: Risk increases with age and certain eye anatomy

conditions.description: Progressive clouding of the eye's crystalline lens that reduces visual quality.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually gradual over months to years and painless.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Painless progressive visual blur and glare with lens opacity support cataract.
important_negative
Sudden visual loss, pain or redness is not typical cataract.
red_flags: Sudden vision loss, flashes/floaters with a curtain, or painful red eye
Requires assessment for another acute eye condition
common_investigations: Confirm lens opacity and assess retina/optic nerve
conditions.diagnostic_context: Examination establishes whether cataract explains the visual impairment; other eye disease may coexist.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Cataract itself is not an emergency.
population_context: Very common with increasing age

conditions.description: A chronic inflammatory condition in which tissue similar to endometrium occurs outside the uterus.

common: Deep pain during or after sex
possible: Pain with bowel movements during periods

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Chronic and variable; symptom severity does not reliably match lesion extent.
risk_factors: early menarche or shorter cycles are associated factors
differentiating_features: characteristic
Cyclical pelvic, bowel or bladder pain supports endometriosis context.
important_negative
A normal ultrasound does not exclude superficial endometriosis.
red_flags: Sudden severe pelvic pain, fainting, heavy bleeding or possible pregnancy
Assess ectopic pregnancy, torsion or other acute causes
common_investigations: Detailed menstrual and pain history with examination
Identify endometrioma or other pelvic pathology
May confirm and treat selected cases
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis can be clinical or surgical depending on context; symptoms overlap with adenomyosis, IBS, pelvic-floor pain and infection.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually chronic; acute severe symptoms require assessment for alternative emergencies.
population_context: Affects people of reproductive age
Symptoms may begin in adolescence

conditions.description: The transition around the final menstrual period caused by declining ovarian follicular function and changing hormone levels.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Perimenopause commonly lasts years; menopause is identified retrospectively after 12 months without menstruation when no other cause exists.
risk_factors: ovarian surgery or some cancer treatments can cause earlier menopause
smoking is associated with earlier timing
differentiating_features: important_negative
Palpitations, bleeding changes or mood symptoms may have other causes and should not automatically be attributed to menopause.
characteristic
Age-appropriate cycle change with vasomotor symptoms is a common transition pattern.
red_flags: Palpitations with collapse, severe chest pain or breathlessness
common_investigations: Often sufficient in otherwise healthy people over 45 with typical symptoms
Targeted pregnancy, blood or hormone testing
Used when younger, atypical or another cause is possible
conditions.diagnostic_context: Life-stage context and menstrual history are central; hormone levels fluctuate and are not always useful in typical midlife transition.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: The transition itself is not an emergency; red-flag bleeding or cardiopulmonary symptoms require separate assessment.
population_context: Natural menopause commonly occurs between ages 45 and 55
Premature ovarian insufficiency requires distinct evaluation

conditions.description: Twisting of the spermatic cord that interrupts blood flow to the testis.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually sudden and progresses over hours; intermittent torsion can produce self-resolving episodes.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Abrupt severe unilateral pain with abnormal testicular lie is highly concerning.
important_negative
Urinary symptoms or preserved cremasteric reflex cannot safely exclude torsion in a concerning presentation.
red_flags: Sudden severe testicular or scrotal pain, especially with swelling or nausea
common_investigations: Used when it will not delay treatment and diagnosis is uncertain
conditions.diagnostic_context: This is time-critical; symptom-index retrieval must not encourage watchful waiting or self-diagnosis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Surgical emergency with time-dependent risk of testicular loss.
population_context: Most common in adolescents but can occur at any age

conditions.description: Infection and inflammation of the upper female genital tract, often associated with sexually transmitted bacteria but sometimes polymicrobial.

possible: Bleeding between periods or after sex

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: May be acute, gradual or mild; delayed treatment increases risk of tubal damage.
differentiating_features: alternative_context
Ectopic pregnancy, appendicitis, ovarian torsion and endometriosis can present similarly.
important_negative
Mild symptoms do not exclude clinically important disease.
red_flags: Severe or worsening pelvic pain, high fever, vomiting, fainting or possible pregnancy
Assess for severe PID or alternative emergency
common_investigations: Used when severe, uncertain or abscess suspected
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis is clinical with a low threshold in at-risk presentations; negative swabs do not exclude upper-tract infection.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Severe infection, pregnancy or suspected abscess requires urgent assessment.
population_context: Affects people with an upper female reproductive tract, typically of reproductive age

conditions.description: Reduced haemoglobin production due to insufficient available iron, usually from blood loss, increased need or inadequate absorption/intake.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually; symptoms depend on severity and rate of decline.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Fatigue alone does not establish iron deficiency.
characteristic
Low ferritin in the appropriate inflammatory context supports depleted iron stores.
red_flags: Chest pain, fainting, severe breathlessness at rest or haemodynamic instability
Possible severe anaemia or active bleeding
Black stool, visible blood, persistent abdominal symptoms or unexplained iron deficiency
common_investigations: Identify anaemia pattern and iron stores
Assess menstrual, gastrointestinal, dietary and malabsorption causes
conditions.diagnostic_context: Laboratory confirmation and investigation of cause are essential; ferritin can rise with inflammation.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Most develops gradually, but severe anaemia or active bleeding may be urgent.
population_context: Higher risk with menstruation and pregnancy
Unexplained deficiency in men or postmenopausal women warrants investigation

conditions.description: Insufficient vitamin B12 causing impaired DNA synthesis and potentially neurological dysfunction.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually; neurological injury can occur with or without marked anaemia and may become irreversible if prolonged.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Serum B12 interpretation can be complex; symptoms alone or an isolated borderline result do not establish deficiency.
alternative_context
Diabetes, thyroid disease and nerve compression can also cause neuropathy.
red_flags: Progressive weakness, gait change, sensory loss or cognitive change
Needs timely assessment to reduce risk of persistent neurological injury
common_investigations: Full blood count and serum B12
Clarify uncertain biochemical cases where available
conditions.diagnostic_context: Interpret tests with symptoms, blood count, folate, kidney function and supplementation history.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually not an emergency, but progressive neurological deficits require prompt review.
population_context: Risk rises with age, restrictive diets and malabsorption

conditions.description: Insufficient folate impairing DNA synthesis and red-cell production.
conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually gradual and depends on intake, absorption, increased requirement or medication effects.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Neurological symptoms are more characteristic of B12 deficiency and B12 status must be considered before folate-only treatment.
alternative_context
Macrocytosis has causes other than folate deficiency.
red_flags: Fainting, chest pain or severe breathlessness with suspected anaemia
common_investigations: Full blood count and serum folate
Assess anaemia pattern and folate status
Avoid missing B12 deficiency and identify driver
conditions.diagnostic_context: Laboratory results require dietary, medication, alcohol, pregnancy and malabsorption context.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually non-emergent; severe symptomatic anaemia changes urgency.
population_context: Requirements increase in pregnancy

conditions.description: Insufficient vitamin D to support normal calcium and bone metabolism; severe deficiency can cause osteomalacia or rickets.

uncommon: Fragility fracture in severe bone disease

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Usually develops gradually and is often detected through risk-based testing rather than symptoms.
differentiating_features: important_negative
Fatigue or diffuse pain alone is not specific for vitamin D deficiency.
characteristic
Biochemical deficiency with compatible bone/mineral findings supports clinical significance.
red_flags: Muscle spasms, seizures, marked tingling or cardiac symptoms with suspected severe deficiency
common_investigations: Assess vitamin D status when testing is indicated
Calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase and parathyroid hormone
Assess significant deficiency or bone disease
conditions.diagnostic_context: Testing and thresholds vary by guideline; symptoms are nonspecific and routine population testing is not always indicated.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Mild deficiency is not an emergency; symptomatic hypocalcaemia is urgent.
population_context: Risk is seasonal and affected by latitude, skin pigmentation, clothing and diet

conditions.description: A chronic pain condition involving widespread pain, sensory amplification and commonly fatigue, sleep and cognitive symptoms.

possible: Sensitivity to touch, sound or light

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Chronic and fluctuating, often with symptom flares; symptoms are real despite absence of a single tissue lesion explaining them.
risk_factors: chronic stress or illness can precede onset
differentiating_features: important_negative
Objective joint swelling, progressive focal weakness, fever or inflammatory organ damage is not explained by fibromyalgia.
alternative_context
Inflammatory, endocrine, sleep and neurological disorders can coexist or mimic parts of the presentation.
red_flags: New focal neurological deficit, true progressive weakness, fever or unexplained weight loss
Assess for an additional condition rather than attributing to fibromyalgia
common_investigations: Clinical pain, sleep and functional assessment
Identify widespread symptom pattern and impairment
Exclude plausible alternatives based on history and examination
conditions.diagnostic_context: A positive clinical diagnosis can coexist with other disease; extensive untargeted testing is not itself diagnostic.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Chronic and non-emergent unless a separate red-flag process is present.
population_context: Can affect any age and sex
More commonly diagnosed in women

conditions.description: A common primary headache disorder typically causing bilateral pressure or tightness without prominent migrainous features.

possible: Either light or sound sensitivity, but usually not both
uncommon: Nausea is atypical for tension-type headache

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Episodes last from tens of minutes to days and may be infrequent or chronic.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Mild-to-moderate bilateral non-throbbing pain without nausea is typical.
important_negative
Sudden onset, fever, neurological deficit, new headache after trauma or progressive pattern requires another explanation.
red_flags: New headache with fever, neck stiffness, persistent neurological change, pregnancy/postpartum context or cancer/immunosuppression
common_investigations: Confirm pattern and screen for secondary causes
Not routine; used when red flags or abnormal examination are present
conditions.diagnostic_context: Diagnosis is clinical after considering migraine and secondary headaches; muscle tension is not required.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Typical recurrent episodes are not emergencies; red-flag headache patterns are.
population_context: Very common across adolescence and adulthood

conditions.description: Inflammation or irritation at rib-to-sternum joints causing localised chest-wall pain.

common: Pain reproducible by pressing the chest wall
Pain worse with upper-body movement or deep breathing
possible: Pain spreading across chest or to back

conditions.typical_onset_and_course: Often self-limited over weeks but can persist or recur.
differentiating_features: characteristic
Focal reproducible tenderness supports chest-wall origin.
important_negative
Reproducible tenderness does not completely exclude cardiac or pulmonary disease when other concerning features exist.
red_flags: Chest pressure with exertion, breathlessness, sweating, fainting, coughing blood or major cardiovascular risk
Assess possible cardiac or pulmonary emergency
common_investigations: Identify reproducible chest-wall pattern and concerning alternatives
Used when acute cardiac, pulmonary or other disease is plausible
conditions.diagnostic_context: A diagnosis of exclusion in the appropriate context; first or concerning chest pain should not be self-labelled costochondritis.
conditions.severity_and_emergency_notes: Usually benign; emergency features relate to alternative causes of chest pain.
population_context: Can affect adolescents and adults
